newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico to start mine exploration rights auctions.
newsitem.headline: Mexico to start mine exploration rights auctions.

text.p: Mexico will publish soon rules for the country's first auctions of mine exploration rights in partially essayed fields in 10 states, the Trade Ministry said Monday.
According to half-complete exploration studies, the fields include deposits of gold, silver, lead, copper, zinc and phosphates.
The mines are across the states of Baja California, Durango, Guerrero, Jalisco, Puebla, Oaxaca, San Luis Potosi, Sinaloa, Sonora and Zacatecas.

"The investors and businessmen who win these auctions will be one step away from a detailed exploration study to quantify the volume of existing reserves in the deposit that they obtain," the ministry said.
The ministry did not state how many fields or parts of fields will be put on the block. It made no mention of exploitation rights.

It is the first time in recent history that Mexico has attempted to sell off mining rights. Normally, companies holding land property titles apply for and are given exploration rights and subsequently exploitation concessions, if deposits are rich.
The ministry said the new mining auctions were an innovative interpretation of mining laws and a way of cashing in on fields discovered by Mexico's Mineral Resources Council.

Two of the first to go to auction will be plots called Reduccion Morelos in the state of Guerrero and El Barqueo in the state of Jalisco, which total 76,000 hectares in surface area. Both have gold deposits, the ministry said.
The ministry said Reduccion Morelos had been divided into two plots and that El Barqueo had been split into three fractions. No timetable was given for the start of the auction procedures.
--Chris Aspin, Mexico City newsroom (525) 7289530. E-mail at chris.aspin@reuters.com
